Link {{< var vm.product >}} records to the agents your teams build in Microsoft Copilot Studio, and bring the results of their Copilot Studio evaluations into the inventory.

## How does the integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio work?

The integration reads from one Copilot Studio environment and does two things:

- **Agent discovery** — Lists the agents in the environment that are not yet linked to a record, so that you can link each one to an existing record, register a new record for it, send it through intake, or ignore it.

- **Evaluation import** — For a linked agent, imports the results of each finished run of a Copilot Studio test set as pass rate metrics on the record.

A connection authenticates in one of two ways:

- **OAuth (user login)** — You sign in with a Microsoft account, and {{< var vm.product >}} reads the agents and their evaluation results on that account's behalf. There is no app registration to create and no client secret to store. This method is offered only where it has been set up for your {{< var vm.product >}} environment.

- **App registration (client secret)** — Your own Microsoft Entra app registration reads the agents. Microsoft only releases evaluation results to a signed-in person, so evaluation import still needs one Microsoft user to sign in on the connection.

Nothing is written back to Copilot Studio.

::: {.attn}

## Prerequisites

- [x] {{< var link.login >}}
- [x] You are a [{{< fa hand >}} Customer Admin]{.bubble} or assigned another role with sufficient permissions to configure connections.[^1]
- [x] You have a Microsoft tenant with Copilot Studio, and a Power Platform environment with Dataverse that contains at least one agent.
- [x] A Microsoft account that can open the agents in Copilot Studio. With OAuth (user login), this account is used to read the agents and their evaluation results.
- [x] To connect with OAuth (user login): if your Microsoft tenant requires admin approval for new apps, an administrator who can approve the {{< var vm.product >}} app.
- [x] To connect with an app registration: you can create an app registration in Microsoft Entra and grant admin consent, and you have the System Administrator role in the Power Platform environment.
- [x] To import evaluation results: Copilot Credits in the environment so that evaluations can run.

:::

## Sync {{< var vm.product >}} records with Microsoft Copilot Studio

With OAuth (user login), setup takes two values from Copilot Studio and a Microsoft sign-in. With an app registration, it also spans Microsoft Entra and the Power Platform admin center.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 1. Set up Microsoft

#### Find the environment details

In Copilot Studio, open **Settings** > **Session details** and copy the **Instance url** and the **Environment ID**.

#### Set up an app registration

Skip the rest of this step if you connect with OAuth (user login).

##### Register an app in Microsoft Entra

a. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **App registrations** and click **New registration**. Choose any name and a single tenant.

b. On the app's **Overview** page, copy the **Application (client) ID** and the **Directory (tenant) ID**.

c. Under **Certificates & secrets**, click **New client secret** and copy the secret's **Value**.

    The value is shown only once. Copy the **Value**, not the **Secret ID**.

##### Allow the app to read evaluation results

Skip these steps if you only need agent discovery and linking.

a. Under **API permissions**, click **Add a permission** and select **APIs my organization uses**.

b. Search for **Power Platform API**.

c. Select **Delegated permissions**, then **CopilotStudio.MakerOperations.Read**, and click **Add permissions**.

d. Click **Grant admin consent**.

##### Add the redirect URI

a. Under **Authentication**, click **Add a platform** and select **Web**.

b. Enter this redirect URI, replacing the first part with the API address of your {{< var vm.product >}} environment:

    ```
    <API URL>/api/v1/integrations/connections/microsoft/oauth/callback
    ```

    The address must match exactly. If you use more than one {{< var vm.product >}} environment, add one redirect URI for each.

##### Add the app to the Power Platform environment

a. In the Power Platform admin center, open **Environments** and select your environment.

b. Go to **Settings** > **Users + permissions** > **Application users**.

c. Click **New app user**, select the app registration, and choose the business unit.

d. Add a security role that can read Copilot Studio agents, then create the user.

### 2. Configure Copilot Studio connection

a. If you connect with an app registration, store its client secret:[^2]

    i. In the left sidebar, click **{{< fa gear >}} Settings**.
    ii. Under {{< fa puzzle-piece >}} Integrations, select **Secrets**.
    iii. Add a secret that holds the client secret value.

b. In the left sidebar, click **{{< fa gear >}} Settings** and, under {{< fa puzzle-piece >}} Integrations, select **Connections**.

c. Click **{{< fa plus >}} Add Connection**.

d. In the modal that opens, select **Microsoft Copilot Studio**.

e. Complete:

   - **Integration Name** — How other admins can identify the connection.
   - **Description** (optional) — The intended usage or additional details.
   - **Authentication Method** — Choose **OAuth (user login)** or **App registration (client secret)**. If only **App registration (client secret)** is listed, OAuth (user login) is not set up for your environment.
   - **Environment URL** — The Instance url from Copilot Studio, for example `https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com`.
   - **Environment ID** — The Environment ID from Copilot Studio.
   - **Initial Status** — Set to `Operational` to enable immediately or `Disabled` if you plan to finish setup later.

    With **App registration (client secret)**, also complete:

   - **Tenant ID** — The Directory (tenant) ID of the app registration.
   - **Client ID** — The Application (client) ID of the app registration.
   - **Client Secret** — The secret that holds the client secret value.

f. Click **Save Integration**.

    You are taken to Microsoft to sign in. Sign in with an account that can open the agents in Copilot Studio. You return to the new connection's details page, which shows the account you signed in with.

    With an app registration, the sign-in is only needed to import evaluation results. If you cancel it, the connection is still saved, and you can sign in later from the connection's **Edit** form.

g. Test the connection:

    i. Hover over the Microsoft Copilot Studio connection you just created.
    ii. When the **{{< fa ellipsis-vertical >}}** menu appears, click on it and select **{{< fa circle-check >}} Test Connection**.

    If the test is successful, the message **{{< fa check-circle >}} Connection successful** displays.

### 3. Link agents to records

a. Click the connection to open its details page.

b. Select the **Unlinked Agents** tab.

    The tab lists the agents in the environment that are not linked to a record yet.

c. Click **{{< fa ellipsis-vertical >}}** next to an agent and choose:

   - **Link to Record** — Link the agent to an existing record. Records of every record type are listed, grouped by type.
   - **Create Record** — Choose a record type. The registration form opens with the agent's name filled in, and the agent is linked once the record is created.
   - **Start Intake** — Open the registration form for your intake record type. Available when your organization has an intake record type.
   - **Ignore Agent** — Remove the agent from the list, with an optional reason.

Linked agents appear on the **Links** tab. Ignored agents appear on the **Ignored Agents** tab with the reason, who ignored them and when, and can be restored from there.

To unlink an agent, open the linked record's **Integrations** tab, find the **Microsoft Copilot Studio** group, and select **Remove Link** from its **{{< fa ellipsis-vertical >}}** menu.[^3]

### 4. Import evaluation results

a. In Copilot Studio, open the agent, go to **Evaluation**, create a test set, and run it.

b. If nobody is signed in to Microsoft on the connection, sign in:

    i. In {{< var vm.product >}}, open the connection's details page and click **Edit this connection to sign in**.
    ii. In the form that opens, click **Sign in with Microsoft** and sign in with an account that can open the agent in Copilot Studio.

    The connection's details page shows the account that evaluation results are imported as.

c. On the connection's details page, select the **Monitoring** tab.

d. Click **Add Evaluation Import**.

e. Select the agent under **Linked Agent** and one of its test sets under **Test Set**, then click **Add Import**.

Each finished run of the test set is imported on a schedule. To import immediately, click **{{< fa ellipsis-vertical >}}** on the import and select **Sync Now**. To stop importing a test set, select **Remove Import** from the same menu; results already imported stay on the record.

For each run, the record receives:

- An overall pass rate — the share of test cases that passed every test method.
- A pass rate for each test method the test set uses, such as General quality, Compare meaning, or Text similarity.

Click a metric name on the **Monitoring** tab to open it on the record. The metrics are listed under **Integration: Copilot Studio**, each named after its test set, for example **Policy Answers Pass Rate**, and charted over time.[^4] To add them to a monitoring document, use **Metric Over Time** > **From Integration**.[^5]

::: {.callout title="Results follow the link"}
Evaluation results are written to the record the import was added on, for as long as the agent stays linked to it. If you remove that link, the import pauses. If the agent is linked to another record, results move there once the original link is removed.
:::

:::

## Change the Microsoft sign-in

The connection's details page shows which Microsoft account is signed in. To sign in as someone else, or to sign in again after a sign-in has expired:

1. On the connection's details page, click **Edit**.

2. Click **Sign Out**, then open the form again and click **Sign in with Microsoft**.

Changing the authentication method, the environment URL or the environment ID of a connection signs it out, as does changing the tenant ID or client ID of an app registration. Deleting a connection also removes its Microsoft sign-in.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The Microsoft sign-in page shows `AADSTS650057` | The app registration has no permission for the Power Platform API. | Add the **CopilotStudio.MakerOperations.Read** delegated permission and grant admin consent. |
| The Microsoft sign-in page shows `AADSTS50011` | The redirect URI is missing or does not match. | Add the redirect URI for this {{< var vm.product >}} environment to the app registration. |
| Connection test: "The Dataverse environment rejected the app" | The app is not an application user in the environment. | Add the app to the Power Platform environment. |
| Connection test: "The app has no permission to read agents in this environment" | The application user's security role is too narrow. | Add a security role that can read Copilot Studio agents. |
| Connection test: "The environment URL did not respond as a Dataverse environment" | The environment URL is wrong. | Use the **Instance url** from Copilot Studio's session details. |
| The run button on Copilot Studio's **Evaluation** tab is disabled | The environment has no Copilot Credits. | Use an environment with Copilot Credits. |
| "The environment ID must be a GUID, or Default-\<tenant ID\> for the default environment" | The connection's environment ID was copied from the wrong field. | Copy the **Environment ID** from Copilot Studio's **Session details** and save the connection. |
| Import: "Microsoft is busy or unavailable" | Microsoft timed out, throttled the request or returned a server error. | Nothing. The import retries automatically over the next few minutes, and again at the next scheduled sync. |
| The Microsoft sign-in ends with "The connection was changed while you were signing in" | The connection's authentication method, tenant ID, client ID, environment URL or environment ID was saved while the sign-in was in progress. | Edit the connection and click **Sign in with Microsoft** again. |
| Import: "ValidMind could not save the results" | {{< var vm.product >}} was briefly unavailable while the results were being saved. | Nothing. The import retries automatically, and again at the next scheduled sync. |
| Import: "No finished evaluation runs for this test set yet" | The test set has not been run, or a run is still in progress. | Run the test set in Copilot Studio, then sync again. |
| Import: "This agent is not linked to a record" | The agent's link was removed. | Link the agent to a record from the **Unlinked Agents** tab. |
| Import: "This agent is now linked to a record that already has an import for this test set" | The agent was linked to another record, which already imports the same test set. | Remove one of the two imports. |
| Import: "Sign in with Microsoft on this connection to import evaluation results" | Nobody is signed in: someone signed out, or the connection's authentication method, tenant ID, client ID, environment URL or environment ID was changed, which signs the connection out. | Edit the connection and click **Sign in with Microsoft**. Results resume within about a minute of signing in. |
| Import: "The Microsoft sign-in on this connection has expired or was revoked" | Microsoft expires a sign-in that is not used for 90 days, or an admin revoked it. | Edit the connection, click **Sign Out**, then sign in again. Results resume within about a minute of signing in. |
| "Sign in with Microsoft on this connection to list its agents" | The connection uses OAuth (user login) and nobody is signed in. | Edit the connection and click **Sign in with Microsoft**. |
| "The Microsoft app has not been granted access to this environment" | The app used to sign in has no consent to read the environment on the signed-in person's behalf. | Ask a Microsoft administrator to approve the app's access to Dynamics CRM (Dataverse), then sign in again. |
| "The signed-in Microsoft user has no permission to read agents in this environment" | The connection uses OAuth (user login), and the signed-in account cannot read agents in the environment. | Sign in with an account that can open the agents in Copilot Studio. |
| "Sign-in without an app registration is not set up on this deployment" | The connection uses OAuth (user login), which is no longer set up for your {{< var vm.product >}} environment. | Edit the connection and switch to an app registration. |

## Limitations

- Evaluation import uses one person's Microsoft sign-in. If that person leaves your organization or their access changes, another admin must sign in on the connection.
- With OAuth (user login), agent discovery uses the same sign-in. The connection lists only the agents that account can see, and stops listing agents while nobody is signed in.
- Microsoft keeps evaluation runs for 89 days. Older runs cannot be imported.
- Pass rates and scores are imported. Individual questions and answers are not.
- Each connection reads one Copilot Studio environment. Add a connection for each environment you want to govern.
